newsitem.title: USA: General Motors Q3 continuing oper net rises.
newsitem.headline: General Motors Q3 continuing oper net rises.

text.p: Oper Shr $1.57 $0.39
Avg shrs primary 756,000 748,200
NOTE: 1995 Q3 net from continuing operations excludes net income of $245.7 million and other income from Electronic Data Systems Corp, which GM spun off in June 1996.
1996 Q3 net from continuing operations includes after-tax gain of $253 million, or $0.34 a share, from reversal of plant closing reserve for Wilmington, Del., assembly plant.
NINE MONTHS
Oper Shr $5.15 $5.21
Avg shrs primary 755,700 749,000
(All data above 000s except per share numbers)

NOTE: 1996 nine months from continuing operations exclude $10 million in net income from EDS after split off costs vs $630.5 million in EDS net income in 1995. 1995 nine months also excludes charge of $51.8 million, or $0.07 a share, for accounting change associated with sales to car rental firms.

Effective tax rate in 1996 Q3 was 2.8 percent, due to lower foreign tax rates, favorable tax settlements and other credits. In the year-ago period, GM received tax benefits from a favorable mix of foreign taxes and income.
Q3 North American Operations and Delphi Automotive Systems Combined net profit $515 million vs loss $93 million.
Q3 International Operations net profit $323 million vs profit $111 million.
Q3 European automotive net profit $75 million vs loss $98 million.
Q3 Net profit margin from continuing operations 3.7 percent vs 1.3 percent.
Q3 cash and marketable securities $14.5 billion vs $8.2 billion.
Q3 worldwide vehicle deliveries 2,085,000 units vs 2,060,000.
Q3 Worldwide vehicle market share 16.1 percent vs 16.9 percent.
Q3 General Motors Acceptance (GMAC) net $307 million vs $254 million.
Q3 Hughes Electronics Corp net $252 million vs $256 million.
